title: Neyphug Kanjur mDo sde Ngi
note: The king or deity Musulundha/Mucilinda acting as a teacher
claim: Musulundha is a king or deity (equated with Mucilinda) acting as a teacher
correction: Musulundha is the king of the gods of the Heaven Free from Strife (Yāma) in the Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna; he is not Mucilinda (the nāga king who sheltered the Buddha). 'King/deity acting as teacher' is right; the '/Mucilinda' equation is wrong.
evidence: 84000 Toh 287 glossary g.950: Musulundha (mu su lun dha) — 'King of the gods in the Heaven Free from Strife' (Yāma heaven); the text has him teach the Dharma to the gods. No equation with Mucilinda.

title: Thadrak Kanjur mDo sde Kha
note: likely a phonetic rendering of a Sanskrit name
claim: Namgru is likely a phonetic rendering of a Sanskrit name
correction: Right that the underlying name is Sanskrit (Raivata), but the Tibetan is a translation of Revati/Raivata rather than a phonetic rendering.
evidence: Nam gru ('boat of the heaven') is the Tibetan translation of Revati (a lunar mansion); the Brahmin Raivata is rendered nam gru, i.e. a semantic translation, not phonetic. Sanskrit name is Raivata (Lalitavistara).

title: Kanjur 'Bum Da
note: Tibetan: ngo bo nyid stong pa nyid; Sanskrit: prakṛti-śūnyatā
claim: ngo bo nyid stong pa nyid = prakṛti-śūnyatā
evidence: ngo bo nyid stong pa nyid is svabhāvaśūnyatā; prakṛtiśūnyatā is rang bzhin stong pa nyid.

title: rNying ma rgyud 'bum Cha
note: likely Garab Dorje's father or a master in the lineage
claim: The Brahmin Sukhamahāsiddha is likely Garab Dorje's father
correction: No source makes a brahmin Garab Dorje's father. In this Yangti lineage (Vajrasattva → the Brahmin → Śrī Siṃha) the brahmin holds the slot of a master before Śrī Siṃha (Garab Dorje/Mañjuśrīmitra position; the cycle is the 'Yang ti bram ze' Brahmin Cycle); the specific person could not be verified.
evidence: Garab Dorje's conception is miraculous (the nun Sudharmā dreams of a white man; tradition names the deity Adhicitta as father); no brahmin is named as his father.

title: Thadrak Kanjur rGyud 'bum Ga
note: referring to Sanskrit as 'mleccha' in this specific context or a non-Tibetan dialect
claim: Sanskrit referred to as 'mleccha' (barbarian language) in this passage
correction: The 'barbarian language' is a non-Sanskrit (foreign) tongue, not Sanskrit.
evidence: Mleccha (Tib. kla klo) means non-Sanskrit speakers/speech; so calling Sanskrit itself mleccha is doubtful, though 'non-Tibetan/foreign dialect' fits.

title: Kanjur dKon brtsegs Kha
note: The personal name of the disciple Shariputra
claim: Śāradvatīputra is the personal name of the disciple Śāriputra
correction: Śāradvatīputra does refer to Śāriputra, but it is a matronymic (son of Śāradvatī), not his personal name; his personal/birth name was Upatiṣya.
evidence: Wikipedia: Śāriputra was born Upatiṣya; Śāradvatīputra is a matronymic ('son of Śāradvatī/Śārikā') honoring his mother.

title: Phurdrup Gonpa Thor bu Nor rgyam chos skor (EAP310-3-3-11)
note: Pema Lingpa (1450–1521) was a major Treasure Revealer (terton) and an incarnation of Guru Rinpoche
claim: He was an incarnation of Guru Rinpoche
correction: Traditionally incarnation of Longchenpa / Princess Pema Sel (a mind-emanation relation to Padmasambhava is at most indirect).
evidence: Article says he was an incarnation of Longchenpa; passage itself says he is reborn Princess Pema Sel (Padmasambhava's disciple), not Guru Rinpoche himself.

title: Neyphug Kanjur mDo sde Ja
note: Tibetan: Blo gros brtan pa; Sanskrit: Sthiramati
correction: Sanskrit should be Dṛḍhamati, not Sthiramati (name equivalence is for the 6th-c. scholar).
evidence: Blo gros brtan pa can be Sthiramati (6th c. scholar), but in the Śūraṃgamasamādhi sūtra the interlocutor Blo gros brtan pa is the bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati (Toh 132).

title: Neyphug Kanjur mDo sde Zha
note: Tibetan: 'Jig rten 'dzin; Sanskrit: Lokeshvara or Jagaddhara
claim: Tibetan 'Jig rten 'dzin = Sanskrit Lokeshvara or Jagaddhara
correction: 'Jig rten 'dzin is Lokadhara. Lokeśvara is 'jig rten dbang phyug (a different figure, Avalokiteśvara); 'Jagaddhara' is not the attested equivalent. The passage (dependent origination addressed to 'World-Holder') matches the Lokadhara sutra.
evidence: 84000 glossary: 'jig rten 'dzin = Sanskrit Lokadhara (Chinese 持世), a bodhisattva and main interlocutor of The Inquiry of Lokadhara (Toh 174), a sutra on aggregates, elements and the twelve links.

title: Neyphug Kanjur rGyud Tsha
note: referring to Vishnu or a specific lineage
claim: 'Son of the Invincible' refers to Vishnu or a specific lineage
evidence: Ajita (Invincible) is a name of Maitreya; the passage lists bodhisattvas, so the figure is Maitreya, not Vishnu.

title: Thadrak Kanjur Kanjur 'Dul ba Tha
note: term: "Me-skyes" gloss: Fire-born, referring to Jivaka Kumarabhritya
correction: me skyes = Jyotiṣka ("Fire-born"), not Jīvaka Kumārabhṛtya ('tsho byed).
evidence: Jivaka's Tibetan name is 'tsho byed; 'fire born' turns up in sources as the epithet of Jyotiska, a different figure, so the note's equivalence is doubtful and unconfirmed.
author_note: Author check: OCR reads མེ་སྐྱེས; 84000 glossary: me skyes = Jyotiṣka. The fire-born child of this Vinaya story is Jyotiṣka; Jīvaka is 'tsho byed. Note (and the running text) misidentify him as Jīvaka.

title: Thadrak Kanjur Kanjur 'Dul ba Tha
correction: Read me skyes (Jyotiṣka, "Fire-born"); "Ajāta / unborn" is wrong.
evidence: Ajata/Ma skyes means unborn in the Ajatashatru name, but the passage says the boy was named for being born from fire, which suggests a fire-born name (Agnijata / me skyes) rather than 'unborn'; no source found for the child's actual name.
author_note: Author check: OCR reads མི་སྐྱེས, a misreading of མེ་སྐྱེས (the passage says he is named for being born from fire). me skyes = Jyotiṣka; the note's "Ajata, unborn" follows the OCR slip.

title: Phurdrup Gonpa Thor bu dPag bsam khri shing
note: Tibetan: dGa' ba'i sde; Sanskrit: Harisena
claim: Tibetan dGa' ba'i sde = Sanskrit Harisena
correction: dga' ba'i sde renders Nandasena ('Joyful Army'), not Harisena (hari = tawny/Vishnu/lion, not joy).
evidence: Sanghata Sutra name appendix: 'Nandasena (Tibetan: dga' ba'i sde or dga' sde) — He Whose Army is Joy'.

title: myur mdzad ye shes kyi mgon po phyag drug pa’i gtor chog bskang gso cha lag dang bcas pa
note: This is the "Sealed Command of Auspiciousness" composed by the Great Siddha Drubchen Nyungpo.
claim: It was composed by the Great Siddha Drubchen Nyungpo
correction: The author is the Great Siddha Khyungpo (Khyungpo Naljor), not 'Nyungpo' — the name is garbled (and 'Great Siddha Drubchen' is redundant: drubchen = great siddha).
evidence: 'This benediction was composed by the Great Siddha Khyungpo' (Khyungpo Naljor, founder of the Shangpa Kagyu).

title: mDo sde stag sna rgyas pa
note: literally: China, but often used for Sanskrit in these contexts
claim: 'In the language of India' literally means China, often used for Sanskrit
correction: rgya gar = India (not China); rgya nag = China.
evidence: rgya gar means India and rgya nag means China; the colophon phrase rgya gar skad du is 'in the language of India' (Sanskrit), so 'literally: China' is incorrect.

title: Dus 'khor 'grel pa dpal gyi sgron me
note: Taurus, Aquarius, Capricorn - though Vessel usually denotes Aquarius, here it refers to the container category
claim: Taurus, Aquarius, Capricorn for Bull, Vessel, Sea-Monster in the Southern Vessel
correction: Southern group should be Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn; Aquarius is already assigned to the West.
evidence: Earth triplicity is Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn (Aquarius is air, and the note itself lists Aquarius in the Western group); the middle sign of the southern group should be Virgo.

title: Srog sgrub snying gi thig le skor
note: A major school of Tibetan Buddhism founded by Atisha
claim: Kadampa is a major school of Tibetan Buddhism founded by Atisha
correction: Founded by Dromtön on the basis of Atisha's teachings; Atisha is its inspirational founding figure.
evidence: Atisha is the most important founding figure, but Dromtön, his disciple, led and institutionalized the school (Radreng, 1056).

title: Rig pa'i rgyal po na ga rag sha'i dbang skor
claim: The passage's 'King of Guides, Gyurme Pelsang' is Minling Terchen Gyurme Dorje
correction: Name in text is Gyurme Pelsang, a different name; identification not supported.
evidence: Minling Terchen's name is Gyurme Dorje, not Gyurme Pelsang; no source links Gyurme Pelsang to him. The note identifies the wrong person for the name in context.
